title: Impact of Drying Techniques on Bonding Strength of Bioceramic Sealers
author: Mohand Saad Mohamed Saeed

steps.title: Collect and disinfect teeth
steps.instruction: Collect extracted human mandibular premolar teeth with a single canal from university clinics (orthodontic, prosthodontic, periodontal extractions). Remove residual soft tissue and calculus, immerse each tooth in 5.25% sodium hypochlorite (Clorox, Egypt) for 5 minutes, then store in sterile saline until use.

steps.title: Verify canal anatomy radiographically
steps.instruction: Take pre‑operative digital radiographs in bucco‑lingual and mesio‑distal directions for each tooth to confirm a single patent canal.

steps.title: Standardize root length
steps.instruction: Cut each tooth under water cooling with a low‑speed Isomet 4000 saw (Buehler, USA) to obtain a uniform root length of 12 mm.

steps.title: Determine working length
steps.instruction: Insert a #10 K‑file (MANI, Inc., 25 mm, Japan) to confirm canal patency. Then insert a #15 K‑file until its tip is visible at the apex; subtract 1 mm to set the standardized working length.

steps.title: Instrument canals
steps.instruction: Instrument each canal with ROGIN Dental VARI‑TAPER Ni‑Ti rotary files (Shenzhen ROGIN Medical Co., Ltd, China) in the sequence: Orifice opener, ISO #15/04, #20/04, #25/04, #30/04, #35/04, and finish shaping to ISO #40/04, following the manufacturer’s settings of 250 rpm and torque ≤ 1.5 N·cm.

steps.title: Irrigate during instrumentation
steps.instruction: After each rotary file, irrigate with 2 ml of freshly prepared 5 % NaOCl (JK Dental, 250 ml, Egypt) delivered through a 30‑gauge side‑vented needle (26 mm, double lateral vents, closed front‑end, Fanta Dental Material Co., Shanghai, China) positioned 1 mm short of the working length. Maintain apical patency between files with a #10 K‑file.

steps.title: Final irrigation and rinse
steps.instruction: Upon completion of instrumentation, irrigate with 2 ml of 17 % EDTA (JK Dental), then flush with 5 ml of sterile saline as the final rinse.

steps.title: Allocate specimens to drying groups
steps.instruction:
Randomly assign the 66 specimens (33 per main group) into three groups (n = 22 each) and their sub‑groups (n = 11 each):
• Group 1 – Dry with Endo‑Aspirator Pro alone (Cerkamed, Poland).
   – Sub‑group 1a: Bio‑C sealer.
   – Sub‑group 1b: Well‑root ST.
• Group 2 – Dry with Endo‑Aspirator Pro followed by sterile paper points.
   – Sub‑group 2a: Bio‑C sealer.
   – Sub‑group 2b: Well‑root ST.
• Group 3 – Dry with sterile paper points only.
   – Sub‑group 3a: Bio‑C sealer.
   – Sub‑group 3b: Well‑root ST.

steps.title: Dry canals according to group
steps.instruction:
For each specimen, apply the assigned drying protocol:
• Endo‑Aspirator Pro alone – insert the aspirator cannula into the canal and activate according to manufacturer instructions.
• Paper‑point drying – insert sterile paper points until the canal appears visually dry.
• Combination – first use the Endo‑Aspirator Pro, then finish with sterile paper points until visually dry.

steps.title: Obturate canals
steps.instruction: Obturate each canal using gutta‑percha (Meta Biomed, China) and the assigned bioceramic sealer (Bio‑C sealer, Angelus, Brazil or Well‑root ST, Vericom, Korea) with the Warm Vertical Compaction technique employing the Fast‑Fill and Fast‑Pack system (Eighteeth, Changzhou Sifary Medical Technology Co., Ltd).

steps.title: Section roots for testing
steps.instruction: After obturation, cut each root horizontally with the Isomet saw under water cooling to obtain three root sections of 1 ± 0.2 mm thickness. Verify slice thickness with a caliper.

steps.title: Perform push‑out bond strength test
steps.instruction: Place each slice on a stainless‑steel plunger in an Instron model 3345 universal testing machine (USA). Apply load in the apico‑coronal direction at a crosshead speed of 1 mm/min until failure occurs. Record the maximum load in Newtons using the BlueHill software.

steps.title: Calculate bond strength
steps.instruction: Convert the recorded load to MPa using: Bond strength (MPa) = N / A, where N is the maximum load (N) and A is the adhesion area (mm²) calculated as A = [π (r₁ + r₂)] × √[(r₁ − r₂)² + h²]; π = 3.14, r₁ and r₂ are the smaller and larger radii of the slice, and h is the slice thickness (mm).

steps.title: Analyze failure mode
steps.instruction:
Examine each failed slice under a stereomicroscope (XCAM 1080P8MPB, ToupTek Photonics, Zhejiang, China) and classify the failure as:
1. Adhesive – no sealer on dentine wall.
2. Cohesive – dentine wall fully covered by sealer.
3. Mixed – both adhesive and cohesive features present.

steps.title: Dispose of specimens
steps.instruction: After testing, sterilize all instruments and teeth specimens and discard them in a designated incinerator under supervision of the microbiology department (Cairo University).
